Φ.name: Phi (potential)
Φ.meaning: A scalar potential, most often the electric potential: the potential energy per unit charge. Its negative gradient is the electrostatic field. Also used for magnetic or gravitational flux and potentials.

τ.name: Tau (time constant)
τ.meaning: A characteristic time: a doubling or decay time, a lifetime, or the proper time measured by a moving clock. Also torque or optical depth in some fields.

δ.name: Delta (small change)
δ.meaning: A small (eventually infinitesimal) increment or variation of a quantity. With two indices, δ_ij is the Kronecker delta: 1 if i = j, 0 otherwise.

∂.name: Partial derivative ∂_μ
∂.meaning: The partial derivative along one coordinate, written as an operator with an index: ∂_μ = ∂/∂x^μ differentiates along spacetime direction μ (0 = time, 1-3 = space).

BH.name: BH⁺ (protonated base)
BH.meaning: Label for a base B that has accepted a proton, BH⁺: the conjugate acid of B. Used as a subscript, e.g. c_BH is the concentration of the protonated form.

χ.name: Chi
χ.meaning: A Greek letter used for an ionisation (binding) energy, a susceptibility, or the Euler characteristic of a surface. In spectra, χ is the energy needed to strip an electron off an atom.

kj.name: Index pair kj
kj.meaning: Two indices together, as for a matrix entry: row k, column j (e.g. symbol j of formula k).

η.name: Eta
η.meaning: A Greek letter for a dimensionless ratio or efficiency - such as the number of baryons per photon in the universe - and for viscosity, or the flat spacetime metric η_μν.
